title: Technical Product Manager
description:
About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

 

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

 

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

 

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

 

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

 

The Role

BJAK is building a Neobank Superapp for Southeast Asia. As a Technical Product Manager, you’ll own a product vertical end to end—such as payments and expense management, remittance, insurance, or wealth and trading—from strategy, outcomes, and roadmap through to the technical design and delivery of the systems behind it.

 

This is a product where real money moves, mistakes are immediately visible, and licensing, compliance, and third-party rails are core product constraints—not considerations around the edges.

 

We are AI-native by default, but AI is a means, not the goal. The bar is knowing where a model can genuinely improve an outcome, where deterministic systems must remain in control, and how to build products that are reliable, auditable, and trusted when money is involved.

 

What you'll be doing

  • Own a vertical end-to-end — outcomes and metrics, a backlog prioritised by value / risk / dependency / strategic priority, acceptance criteria crisp enough to build and test against.

  • Shape the technical design with engineering — system boundaries, money-movement correctness (idempotency, ledgering, reconciliation), third-party-rail reliance and rail-down behaviour, failure/retry/refund paths, security, latency, scalability, recovery.

  • Make hard trade-offs across correctness, speed, cost, reliability and UX — and defend them to an engineering, compliance or ops lead who pushes back.

  • Treat regulated constraints as first-class product inputs — licensing scope, CDD/KYC and limits, sanctions/PEP screening, transaction monitoring, data residency and privacy. Know which are hard launch gates and which are forward-readiness.

  • Apply AI where it earns its place — define what it's allowed to decide, where a human stays in the loop, how it's evaluated, and what it does when unsure. Every AI-surfaced number traces back to a real record.

  • Ship against external gates — build feature-complete behind flags; go live per rail as each partner and regulatory gate clears.

  • Work across Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance/Reconciliation.

     

What you'll need

  • Product leadership — significant experience owning a complex technical product end-to-end; strong judgement and decisiveness under ambiguity; ability to balance ambition against technical, regulatory and operational reality; can hold their own with senior engineers.

  • Technical foundation — solid system design (boundaries, datastores, queues/workflows, APIs, failure modes, consistency under concurrency); comfort reading, reviewing and challenging design docs; can sketch an architecture and a sequence. No production code, but technical enough that engineers don't have to simplify.

  • Domain — experience in a regulated / high-consequence domain (payments, banking, remittance, insurance, …) or demonstrable fast-ramp ability; understands why money movement is different (correctness over convenience, irreversible states, partners you don't control).

  • AI judgement — hands-on with LLM-based products; can frame a feature as eval-able (offline, online, human feedback); realistic on hallucination/drift/data gaps, including data-blocked vs model-blocked and when a model must not be in the loop at all.

  • Nice to have — engineer or highly-technical-PM background · zero-to-one · shipped AI-heavy consumer products · defined eval metrics for ML/LLM systems · AI UX + failure-handling intuition · SEA market experience.

     

Outcomes

  • Clear vertical strategy and legible roadmap

  • Ships fast and clears the gates that actually block launch

  • Money is correct and users are never misled about the state of their funds

  • AI features are valuable, predictable and trusted

  • Trade-offs made deliberately under uncertainty and hold up when challenged

  • Engineering, design, compliance, and operations are aligned with minimal friction

     

Location

This role is remote, but candidates must be based in Germany. We are hiring specifically for this market, so applicants should already be based in Germany.

 

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

 
 

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

1. Online assessment or practical task

2. Role-specific interview

3. CEO / final round

 

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

title: Business Development Director (DACH)
description:
About the Role 

Imagine this. You are the person German, Austrian and Swiss defence customers call first when they want to understand what is actually possible, and the person inside Destinus who turns that conversation into a funded programme. 

At Destinus, we are revolutionizing the defense industry with cutting-edge Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). Our innovative technologies are designed to meet the unique demands of modern defense operations, delivering unparalleled speed, precision, and cost effectiveness. Destinus partners with government agencies and defense organizations worldwide to provide advanced solutions for mission-critical operations, enabling a new era of efficiency and technological superiority. Join us in shaping the future of defense with groundbreaking aerospace innovations. 

This role sits in the Future Capabilities organisation of Destinus Germany and reports to the Chief Future Capabilities Officer. You lead senior business development for the DACH region and open the doors that future capability programmes need in order to exist at all. 

You will build the DACH BD team. The measure of this role is the forces commitments that turn advanced technology into procurement-ready capability for the region. You work as one team across the company: with Commercial on pricing, contracting and pipeline, with Engineering on what is technically achievable.  

 

What You’ll Do 

  • Build and lead senior business development for Germany, Austria and Switzerland, covering armed forces, procurement authorities, security agencies and industrial partners. 
  • Open and hold senior access at BMVg, BAAINBw, Bundeswehr commands, national agencies and NATO bodies, in close coordination with Destinus government relations. 
  • Shape future demand: translate what customers and users actually need into requirements input the capability teams can build against. 
  • Run capture for DACH opportunities from qualification through to first customer commitment, together with Commercial on the commercial shape and with Engineering on what is technically achievable. 
  • Build, lead and develop a team of business developers, and set the standard for how Destinus shows up in front of German customers. 
  • Work as one commercial motion with the Commercial organisation: one CRM, one pipeline, every opportunity visible to everyone who needs it. 
  • Own joint account plans for the key DACH accounts 
  • Feed a clear and honest view of the DACH market back into portfolio and capability decisions. 

Requirements

What You’ll Need 

  • Substantial senior business development or capture experience in defence, security or adjacent deep technology, with a record of closing first commitments. 
  • Deep working knowledge of German defence procurement: how requirements form, how budget lines come about, how tenders and framework contracts run, and where decisions are actually made. 
  • An established senior network across BMVg, BAAINBw, the Bundeswehr, national agencies, research organisations and German industry. 
  • The ability to hold your own in a technical discussion and to bring engineers into a customer conversation at the right moment. 
  • Proven ability to deliver in a matrix organisation, building strong working relationships across commercial, engineering and programme teams. 
  • Experience building, leading and developing small senior teams, including hiring. 
  • Aerospace and defence industry experience is mandatory. 
  • Fluency in English and German is required. 

 

Who You Are  

You are comfortable being early. This is a build role in a young organisation, and much of the structure around you will be created as you go. You are a translator by instinct, between operator and engineer, between customer need and product concept, between Germany and a European group. You qualify hard and early, and you are straight with colleagues and customers about what you see. You enjoy the matrix and you bring people from other functions with you. You hold yourself to what you promised a customer, and you travel to be in the room when it matters.

title: Automation Engineer - PLC / Plant Control (m/f/d)
description:
ABOUT US

METYCLE - where innovation meets sustainability

We are building the B2B online platform to accelerate the global circular flow of secondary metals. By connecting buyers and sellers of scrap metal globally, we enable efficient trade of secondary metals and drive the seamless flow of recycling material, essential for reducing CO2 emissions by up to 95% compared to primary metal production.

And we take it further! We are pioneering an innovative Smart Sorting Facility that leverages AI, machine learning, and robotics to transform how scrap metal is processed, enhance material quality, improve traceability, and drive the recycling industry into the digital era.

Join us at the early stage in bringing the $610 billion scrap metal trading industry into the 21st century and in shaping the future of metal recycling and green energy solutions.


READY TO MAKE AN IMPACT?

If you are passionate about industrial automation, solving complex technical challenges, and building something from the ground up, join our team as an Industrial Automation Engineer.

The machinery is the easy part to buy. The control system that turns it into a plant - and the standards, documentation, and data that keep it running - is what we are hiring you to own.

We are looking for an experienced Industrial Automation Engineer to take ownership of our plant’s control systems from design through commissioning and into stable production. You bring deep hands-on experience in programming and commissioning industrial control systems and are comfortable taking responsibility for the PLC, safety systems, HMI, industrial networking, and interfaces between multiple machine suppliers.

Beyond programming, you understand what it takes to make a plant genuinely reliable in production and have the technical confidence to hold suppliers to high professional standards. Join our international team, help build innovative solutions for scrap metal processing, and contribute to a more sustainable future.


YOUR MISSION

  • PLC & Plant Control: Design, write, and own the PLC program using Siemens TIA Portal / S7-1200 & S7-1500, including control logic, sequencing, fault handling, and HMI
  • Commissioning & Production: Take the plant from design through commissioning to a stable, running line, owning the full journey through FAT/SAT and the hands-on work required to make the plant genuinely reliable
  • Plant Availability: Design stop and interlock behaviour to minimise unnecessary downtime — allowing unaffected parts of the plant to keep running when it is safe to do so. Plant availability is a direct business outcome here, and you will directly influence it
  • Machine Safety: Implement the machine-safety control concept on a fail-safe F-CPU with F-I/O, including the hardwired e-stop loop, PLC-enforced zone isolation that cannot be overridden, guard interlocks, and controlled, sequenced shutdown
  • Safety & Compliance: Be our in-house technical counterpart on EN ISO 13849 performance-level determination and the CE file, working with external assessors while retaining ownership of the technical approach and decisions
  • Machine Integration: Integrate control systems from several different machine suppliers into one coherent line, so that a single stop is genuinely a single stop across the whole plant
  • Supplier Management: Hold machine builders and panel builders to specification, including unlocked code, complete documentation, and standards compliance
  • OT / IT & Industrial IoT: Get plant data out over OPC UA / MQTT / Modbus TCP into our own systems, so stoppage reasons, energy use, and throughput become actionable data. Work closely with our Industrial IoT team, who own the edge and data side of that boundary


YOUR PROFILE

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience programming and commissioning industrial control systems, with a track record of bringing production equipment or complete lines into stable operation
  • Deep Siemens TIA Portal / S7-1200 & S7-1500 experience, with strong skills in SCL, LAD/FBD, HMI/SCADA, industrial networking (PROFINET, PROFIBUS, Modbus TCP), drives/VFDs, and fault-finding
  • Strong machine safety competence, including F-CPU / Safety Integrated and EN ISO 13849, with the ability to explain and defend performance-level determinations
  • Comfortable reading electrical schematics and troubleshooting cabinets, hardware, signals, wiring, and control behaviour directly on the shop floor. You have brought at least one production line from commissioning into stable production; maintenance-only experience is not sufficient
  • Experience working with machine and panel builders, with the confidence to hold suppliers accountable for code quality, documentation, standards compliance, and professional delivery
  • Experience with brownfield projects and legacy migration (STEP 7 Classic → TIA); experience in bulk material handling, recycling, sorting, or minerals processing is a plus
  • Experience with PLC version control, simulation / digital twins, or structured automation approaches is desirable. Additional IT/OT skills such as Python, C#/TIA Openness, SQL, Linux, Docker, MES/IIoT, OT network segmentation, or IEC 62443 are a plus
  • Independent, structured, and hands-on, with a strong sense of ownership. You challenge assumptions, hold suppliers to a high standard, and document what you build
  • Fluent in English; German and/or Dutch is a plus. Ideally based in or near Cologne or the Benelux/border region, with valid EU work authorisation and the willingness to travel to our Smart Sorting Facility in Belgium, Maasmechelen

Working at Deliveroo is the perfect environment to build a definitive career, motivated by impact on your own development, on Deliveroo as we scale, and on the marketplace and communities we serve.

Consumer Ordering Experience owns the core purchase journey: the store page, item page, basket, and checkout flow, across both app and web. It's a global team — the surfaces we build support all of our brands: Deliveroo, Wolt, and Doordash. You'd be the team's first dedicated web/full-stack engineer, helping us build out our web experience from the ground up.

What You'll Do

  • Own and evolve the store, item, basket, and checkout experiences on web, working primarily in React and TypeScript
  • Contribute to backend services written in Golang — deep Go experience isn't a hard requirement, but you should be comfortable picking up a new statically typed backend language
  • Improve code structure, shape architecture, and review code across the team
  • Partner closely with your Product Manager and fellow engineers to scope and ship changes to the ordering funnel
  • Take part in the hiring process and support the growth of your teammates as the team scales

 

What We're Looking For

Must haves:

  • Strong full-stack experience — comfortable working across web frontend (React/TypeScript) and backend (Go, or similar) to unblock delivery end-to-end
  • Experience designing, implementing and rolling out A/B experiments (or strong aptitude to quickly learn our experimentation platform) — including guardrail metrics, staged rollouts and reading results
  • Comfortable operating in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment with shifting priorities and short XP cycles (weeks, not quarters)
  • Strong ownership mindset — able to take a brief PRD through design, implementation, rollout and production monitoring with minimal hand-holding
  • Track record of shipping incrementally and iterating on data rather than big-bang launches
  • Willing to participate in an on-call rotation and respond to incidents

 

Nice to haves:

  • Experience coordinating engineers across multiple platforms (iOS/Android/Web/BE) on a single initiative
  • Active use of AI-assisted coding workflows, and interest in building reusable tooling/skills for the team

 

We're looking for someone London-based who can work from our office 2–3 days a week alongside the rest of the team.

At Deliveroo, you'll do work that matters—solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that's constantly evolving. 🧠 Grow through challenge and ownership Take on big, ambiguous problems and accelerate your career with strong support.

🌎 A culture built for builders High standards, collaboration, flexible working and continuous learning.

💰 Share in the success you help create Competitive salary and equity options, so you're rewarded for the impact you make.

title: Legal Counsel
description:
Who we are:

We're one of Europe's fastest-growing fintech companies – on a mission to create the world's most empowering way to pay.

We launched the product in 2020 and achieved double unicorn status, valued at $2 billion, and since then have taken on more than 6 million customers.

 

Our mission is to become the best way to pay for anything, anywhere and say goodbye to credit costs for everyone. This is huge. Want to join us?

About the role.

We are looking for a dynamic Legal Counsel, with circa 1-4 years PQE, to play a vital role in providing legal support and advice to our organisation as we continue to expand our operations in the UK and internationally. You will work closely with other members of our Legal team and teams across the business to advise on a broad range of legal matters, including arrangements with our commercial partners, corporate transactions and governance initiatives, and help ensure that we continue to comply with relevant laws and regulations in the UK and across international markets.

You’ll have an interest in a varied workload, with strong drafting and negotiating skills, sound commercial judgment, and the ability to balance legal risk with business priorities. You’ll be proactive and hands-on in your approach, happy to get stuck into a broad range of legal work, able to work independently while knowing when to escalate, and capable of building trust with business teams.

In addition, you’ll have a focus on developing and maintaining the legal processes, policies and precedents that underpin our business.

This is a fantastic opportunity if you enjoy operating in a fast-paced, growing business where priorities can change quickly, and are looking to take real ownership for what you do.

Day to day responsibilities.

  • Work with our business teams to draft, review and negotiate a wide range of commercial agreements, and other legal documents with third parties, including our key suppliers and partners, whilst maintaining the processes that underpin them.

  • Support with corporate matters including acquisitions, capital raising, group structure and integration projects, international expansion, debt arrangements and employee share schemes.

  • Support with governance and investor relations initiatives, including the preparation of board and committee papers and resolutions, updating our cap table and maintaining internal trackers.

  • Assist in resolving legal disputes, including working with external counsel when necessary.

  • Be a trusted legal advisor to our commercial teams to help establish, maintain, and expand business relationships whilst providing input into new products and initiatives.

  • Identify legal risks and propose strategies to mitigate them.

  • Support the consideration and implementation of new legal tech tools and the development and maintenance of processes, policies and procedures and standard legal documents.

  • Conduct legal research on various topics, including emerging legal issues which may impact our business, and provide recommendations to the legal team and senior management.

  • Develop and deliver legal training programmes to internal teams to ensure awareness of legal and regulatory requirements.

Key requirements:

  • Ideally, 1-4 years PQE.

  • A current practising certificate (qualified in England and Wales is preferred).

  • Meaningful and relevant experience either from private practice or in-house.

  • Experience gained in a fintech or another fast-paced technology business or internationally would be a bonus, but otherwise you should be able to demonstrate enthusiasm for gaining that experience.

  • Solid drafting, reviewing, negotiation and problem-solving skills.

  • Solutions-focused attitude, with a commercial-minded risk appetite.

  • Excellent attention to detail.

  • Strong stakeholder and time-management skills, including the ability to manage competing priorities

title: Electrical Engineer II (Integrations)
description:
Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe!

Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy.

We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide.

It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.

🐙 Kraken Generation Flex

The energy industry is undergoing the largest transformation since industrialisation, at an unprecedented rate of change and we are positioning ourselves at the heart of it. In the UK, with a legally binding Net Zero target for 2050 and a clean-power ambition for 2030, we are scaling rapidly to integrate Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) into the grid.

Kraken is recognised as a thought leader and innovator. With complete independence from Octopus Energy, we are building a SaaS business that digitally connects hundreds of thousands of DERs with energy markets. As our UK fleet grows and we support our expansion across Europe, we are looking for an Integrations Engineer to help turn customer sites into market-connected, controllable assets.

🏠 Where you’ll fit in and role summary

As we scale our fleet of integrated assets, we are looking for an Electrical Engineer to support the delivery of our site integrations and grow into owning them, learning the full lifecycle from the early information stage through design, deployment and testing.

You’ll be part of an engineering delivery team, based in Manchester, who take an integration project from the very early information stage, design how it will be integrated into Kraken’s platform and then turn that design into a live, controllable, market-participating asset.

Engineering delivery is an innovative and engineering-focused team with a culture that fosters collaboration and fresh thinking to create a new energy system. Alongside design, deployment and testing; they constantly look into ways to improve efficiency through tooling and the automation of repetitive tasks. They collaborate daily with delivery managers and customer success to onboard new sites as well as support the existing.

🚀 What you'll own

  • Integration design contribution: With guidance, analyse provided information and contribute to hardware and software integration approaches. When necessary, exchange information with customer technical representatives through meetings and emails, and take part in design discussions with other team members.

description:

It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.

🏡 Where you'll fit in:
KrakenFlex is the flexibility arm of the Kraken group, built to put a big green dent in global carbon emissions by rewriting how electricity grids operate. We stabilize the grid and help renewables come online much faster by managing the second-by-second balance of clean power. Right now, our platform connects nearly one million assets worldwide, putting over 6GW of live load under our direct control.

Behind the scenes, that means handling massive technical scale: solving complex optimization problems in real time and processing 15 billion data readings a day from the latest green technologies, ensuring the grid stays reliable without relying on old fossil-fuel backup plants.

The next phase of our journey involves monumental growth. Currently operational across multiple countries, we are poised for further global expansion, scaling our asset base and tackling unique grid challenges in new territories. Our mission is to integrate an increasingly diverse array of green flexibility assets while ensuring our market-leading platform remains exceptionally stable and performant.

What is Optimisation in Flex?
The Optimisation chapter is the mathematical and algorithmic engine of the KrakenFlex platform. While other chapters manage physical asset connectivity or ingest market signals, this domain is responsible for the intelligence that decides exactly what every asset should do, second by second, to maximise both grid stability and financial returns.

The teams within this chapter build and maintain the real-time dispatch engines, predictive forecasting models, and algorithmic solvers that handle massive multi-asset portfolios. This involves translating complex market rules, physical asset constraints (like battery degradation curves, state-of-charge limits, and ramp rates), and fluctuating price signals into optimised execution strategies.

The defining challenge for this chapter is scaling computational performance alongside our rapid asset growth. Running complex, multi-variable mathematical models in tight real-time windows requires immense efficiency. The core tension lies in balancing the demand from data science and quantitative engineering to introduce increasingly sophisticated models with the strict platform requirement for absolute reliability, low latency, and cost-effective cloud compute.

Ultimately, this chapter must move away from bespoke optimisation routines tailored to individual markets or asset types. Your goal is to architect a highly performant, modular optimisation core that uses standard abstract layers, allowing us to roll out new algorithms or expand into new global territories without rewriting the underlying engine.

🚀 What you’ll own:
The Flex platform is built on autonomous Chapters, which are collections of specialists focused on delivering a core service or business outcome, defined by the unchanging nature of the energy business (independent of technology, hardware, or regional differences). A Head of Engineering leading a Chapter is a senior leadership role combining strong product thinking, engineering judgement, operational awareness, and people leadership. They manage managers and senior individual contributors, helping teams own their product surfaces, make sound trade-offs, and deliver reliably.

This role requires influencing beyond its formal remit, spotting cross-team patterns, clarifying ownership and decision-making, and driving initiatives to turn recurring issues into visible actions with owners, dates, and measures of success. Ultimately, they maintain the technical vision for their specific area, ensuring services are appropriately owned, maintained, and aligned with Flex's sustainable growth.

  • Ensuring the appropriate level of quality and resilience, with a specific focus on reducing system incidents and improving stability.

  • Ensuring appropriate tech debt is prioritised to support sustainable delivery.

  • Potentially managing a squad (team) as well.

🧠 What you’ll bring to the party:
You’ll be a strong fit if you have experience leading engineering teams across multiple squads, teams or product areas in a complex product environment.

  • Strong judgement in ambiguity: you can separate urgent from important, make trade-offs explicit and help teams move without pretending all uncertainty has disappeared.

About The Role

The Finance Business Partner will be embedded within the Project Controllership Organization, acting as the finance owner for large, long-duration capital projects from initial commitment through to completion and transfer to operations. You will bring rigorous project and cost accounting to the delivery teams: owning capex and cost accounting for your projects, building and maintaining project cost structures, tracking budgets, commitments and actuals, reporting variances with insight, and ensuring each project is accounted for accurately under US GAAP and closed out cleanly at completion. This is a hands-on role that pairs technical accounting depth with genuine business partnering - you will sit alongside project directors, engineers and procurement, not apart from them.

What You Will Be Doing

Project and capex accounting

  • Capex accounting: own end-to-end accounting for assigned capital projects, including construction in progress (CIP/AUC), capitalization assessments under US GAAP (ASC 360), componentization, capitalized interest where applicable (ASC 835-20), and transfer to fixed assets on completion with correct in-service dates and useful lives.

  • Compute and equipment capex: own the accounting for high-value compute and network equipment (GPU fleets and associated infrastructure), including vendor purchase order and financing payment tracking, delivery acceptance and in-service dating, componentization and useful lives, residual value support, and lessor accounting for intra-group equipment leases (ASC 842).

  • Cost accounting: maintain accurate, complete and well-classified project cost records - distinguishing capital from operating expenditure, applying the capitalization policy consistently, and ensuring costs land in the correct entity, project, site and cost category.

  • Project costing: build and own project cost breakdown structures (WBS/cost codes) aligned to contracts, procurement packages and the accounting dimension framework; establish cost baselines and estimates-at-completion (EAC) and keep them current.

  • Accruals and commitments: run monthly cost accruals from contractor applications for payment, certifications and goods receipts; maintain the committed cost position (POs, contracts, change orders) and reconcile committed, accrued and actual spend.

  • Month-end close: deliver project close activities to the group timetable - CIP reconciliations, accrual journals, retention and milestone payment tracking, and balance sheet substantiation for project-related accounts.

Reporting, variance analysis and forecasting

  • Variance reporting: produce monthly project cost reports comparing actuals and EAC against budget and prior forecast; explain variances with root-cause commentary and work with project teams on corrective actions.

  • Forecasting: partner with FP&A and Strategic Finance on capex cashflow forecasting, phasing of spend, and funding drawdown planning for your projects. Provide current capex phasing and estimate-at-completion data into Strategic Finance's monthly business plan refresh.

  • Board and investor reporting: contribute project cost and progress data to board packs, lender/investor reporting and management information, ensuring one version of the truth between delivery and finance. Work within, and help build, the group project reporting framework.

  • Balance sheet visibility: own the project-related balance sheet - CIP, retentions, VAT recoverable, prepayments and committed spend - and feed these positions into the group management balance sheet dashboard on an automated, near-real-time basis.

Project lifecycle and business partnering

  • Cradle to completion: support projects through their full lifecycle - business case and budget setting, contract award, execution, change management, practical completion, final account settlement, and financial close-out including release of retentions and accrual true-ups.

  • Change control: evaluate the cost and accounting impact of scope changes, change orders and claims; ensure changes are approved, coded and forecast before costs are incurred.

  • Business partnering: act as the trusted finance counterpart to project directors, construction managers, procurement and engineering; challenge constructively, translate financial data into decisions, and embed cost discipline in delivery teams.

  • Contract and procurement support: work with procurement and legal on the financial aspects of construction and equipment contracts (payment mechanisms, milestones, retentions, bonds, liquidated damages) and ensure compliance with the Group Procurement Policy and PO controls.

Controls, policy and audit

  • Controls: operate and help design internal controls over project costs, capitalization and payments as part of the group's SOX 404 readiness program, including preparing clear documentation and audit evidence.

  • Policy: apply and help refine group accounting policies (capitalization, PP&E, procurement) and prepare technical accounting analysis for project-specific matters, escalating judgmental issues with well-structured recommendations.

  • Audit: act as the primary project-accounting contact for external audit on assigned projects, preparing schedules, reconciliations and supporting evidence.

  • Anything else that makes sense: as an early hire in a fast-scaling finance function, contribute to systems implementation (ERP selection ongoing), process design, and whatever else is needed to build best-in-class project controllership.

What You Bring

  • Qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CPA or equivalent) with strong post-qualification experience.

  • Demonstrable experience of project accounting for large, long-term capital projects - for example data centers, energy, utilities, infrastructure, construction or industrial facilities - covering the full project lifecycle.

  • Deep, practical knowledge of capex and cost accounting: CIP/AUC, capitalization criteria, componentization, accruals from contractor valuations, retentions, and asset transfer at completion.

  • Experience building and managing project cost structures (WBS/cost coding), budgets, committed cost tracking and estimates-at-completion.

  • Strong variance analysis and reporting skills, with the ability to explain cost movements clearly to non-finance stakeholders.

  • Proven business partnering experience embedded with, or working closely alongside, project delivery teams.

  • Advanced Excel and strong data and dashboarding skills, with an automation-first mindset; comfortable working from imperfect data in a scaling environment.

Nice To Have

  • US GAAP experience (ASC 360 fixed assets, ASC 835-20 capitalized interest, ASC 842 leases as they touch project sites).

  • Experience in a SOX-regulated or IPO-readiness environment, or supporting external audits of major capital projects.

  • Exposure to multi-entity, multi-currency structures and cross-border projects.

description:
About Volta

Volta is the category-defining, fully vertically integrated AI infrastructure platform – from capital to clusters to software, under a founder-led enterprise. Our mission is The Utility of Compute™: AI infrastructure as dependable and available as electricity, for every organization that needs it. Launched with a $10B strategic partnership with one of the leading frontier AI labs, a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz, and a $5B AI Infrastructure Fund, Volta is building the infrastructure layer of the AI era from the ground up. We are 100+ people across London, Palo Alto, and New York, with rapid growth expectations to hundreds.

About The Role

Volta builds and operates large scale GPU compute infrastructure for AI workloads. Our platform is Kubernetes-native, spans multiple regions, and delivers virtual machines, storage, and networking through a fully automated infrastructure stack built on custom Kubernetes operators.

We are building out several platform engineering teams that together own the full stack, from managed bare metal and IaaS through to higher-order platform services. Each team owns a different part of that stack: compute, networking, storage, the control plane and API layer, confidential computing, and the customer-facing surface. The area you work in depends on the team you join and your prior expertise, so no single engineer is expected to cover all of it.

Platform Engineers work at the intersection of infrastructure and software development. Across every team, you will translate three key inputs into durable platform capabilities: product roadmap requirements from the product team, operational learnings from the bring-up teams, and security guidance from the security engineering team. The output of this role is production platform code, not configuration, not runbooks.

 

What You Will Be Doing

Common across every platform engineering team:

  • Design and implement Kubernetes operators and controllers that manage the lifecycle of platform resources.

  • Work closely with the product team to turn roadmap requirements into the platform capabilities that support them.

  • Collaborate with the bring-up teams to identify operational pain points and turn them into scalable platform features.

  • Integrate security guidance from the security engineering team into platform-level controls, and remediate findings at the platform layer.

  • Treat observability as a platform concern: instrument services, define meaningful metrics, and build tooling that gives the team visibility into platform health.

  • Own the services you build in production, including participation in an on-call rotation, incident response, and the follow-up work that closes structural gaps rather than only the immediate issue.

  • Hold to clean interface and versioning practice on anything other teams or customers depend on, including disciplined handling of breaking changes.

  • Participate in code review, technical design discussions, and cross-team collaboration in an Agile (Kanban or Scrum) environment.

Depending on your team and background, you will go deep in some of the following:

  • Control plane and APIs: improve and extend the API layer between user-facing services and the underlying platform, with disciplined versioning and backward compatibility.

  • Compute: build and operate the lifecycle of virtualized and bare metal compute resources.

  • Storage: provisioning workflows, attachment reliability, performance tuning, and failure handling.

  • Confidential computing: build and extend confidential computing capabilities across the stack, from secure bare metal and confidential VMs to Confidential Containers (CoCo).

  • Customer-facing services: the platform surfaces customers interact with directly, including the APIs and interfaces through which they consume capacity, working alongside product and UX.

 

What You Bring

  • 3 to 5 years of software engineering experience, with a meaningful portion spent on infrastructure or platform systems.

  • Strong backend or systems programming experience in a production environment. Our working languages are Python, Go, and Rust; we welcome strong engineers from other compiled or object-oriented languages (for example C++, C#, or Java) who are ready to work across our stack as it evolves.

  • Solid understanding of Kubernetes internals: the control loop model, CRDs, controllers and operators, and reliable reconciliation logic.

  • Comfortable working close to the infrastructure layer: Linux, networking fundamentals, and distributed systems behavior.

  • Experience designing, building, and versioning production-grade APIs or service interfaces that other teams depend on, including disciplined handling of breaking changes and backward compatibility.

  • Experience operating what you build: debugging production systems, and taking part in on-call or incident response.

  • Strong engineering fundamentals: clean code, testing, version control, code review, and CI/CD practices.

Nice to Have (But Not Essential)

None of these are required. Several map to specific teams, so strength in one or more helps us match you to the right one:

  • Fluency with AI-assisted development: agentic CLI tools, IDE assistants, and orchestrating multiple coding agents through MCP, skills, or APIs to amplify delivery.

  • Depth in Go or Rust beyond working proficiency.

  • Familiarity with confidential computing technologies: TEEs, AMD SEV, Intel TDX, or Confidential Containers (CoCo).

  • Experience integrating security requirements into platform or infrastructure systems.

  • Familiarity with high-performance networking: overlay protocols, BGP, RDMA, or packet-processing frameworks.

  • Hands-on experience with distributed storage systems (Ceph or similar) at an engineering level.

  • Background building Kubernetes operators using frameworks such as Kopf, controller-runtime, or similar.

  • Experience with observability tooling: Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, or structured logging in distributed systems.

  • Experience building SaaS or PaaS layers on top of an IaaS platform.

  • Exposure to serverless or inference serving infrastructure.

description:
Lead Product Designer

📍 Manchester (Hybrid, up to 4 days WFH)

💰 £70k-£90k (negotiable)

Street Group is one of the fastest-growing PropTech companies in the UK. We want to be the leading creator of delightful experiences for everybody involved in buying, selling, renting and letting property, regardless of their involvement, to improve the industry for everybody by elevating UK Estate Agencies through world-class technology.

We're now looking for a Lead Product Designer - the most senior individual contributor for design within a product domain. This is predominantly an IC role: you'll set the design bar for an entire domain through the quality of your own work, the patterns you contribute, and the way you raise the designers around you. We're flexible on this for the right person, if you've got management experience, or want to line-manage one or two designers alongside the IC work, let's talk.

We want someone who is tired of the "feature factory" grind, who is past needing to be told what's worth working on, and who is ready to set the design direction for a domain in one of the most exciting PropTech companies in the UK.

If you look at most UX job ads, you see a laundry list of requirements. We prefer to tell you how we actually operate so you can decide if this is the right environment for you.

  • At Street Group, design is a strategic seat. Lead Product Designers drive roadmap conversations alongside their product and engineering counterparts, not respond to them.

  • Our users rely on us to run their businesses, so they love talking to us. You can spin up a call and validate a prototype instantly. We don't guess; we ask.

  • We move at pace, including on strategic work. Strategy isn't a separate, slower track here - we test it by shipping.

Here's what you can expect to be working on as an L6 Lead Product Designer at Street Group

  • Own the design vision and execution for a product domain. Translate strategic direction into the most ambiguous, cross-cutting, or strategically important pieces of design work.

  • Set the craft bar through your own output. The work you ship is the reference point for what good looks like in your area.

  • Own the cross-cutting design problems: patterns across multiple features, flows across multiple surfaces, the coherence of the domain's experience as a whole.

  • Mentor and raise the bar of the designers around you - through critique, pairing, and modelling what excellent design looks like.

  • Drive AI thinking strategically - both in your own workflow (Claude Code, in-product changes, prototype testing) and in what we ship to users. You'll have a strong view on what makes a good AI feature in this domain vs a gimmicky one.

Why you should (and shouldn't) apply

You should apply if:

  • You've operated at senior IC level in a modern product org and you want broader scope to influence what gets built.

  • You're commercially fluent. You've made design trade-offs informed by how the product makes money, not just by user preference. You can name those trade-offs and defend them either way.

  • You define what success looks like before you ship, and you read the result against it after. Metrics, support data, customer feedback - you go and look.

  • You have strong, well-formed views on AI in product design and have put them into practice. You can articulate when AI is the right design solution and when it isn't.

  • You move at pace on strategic work, not just on features.

You probably shouldn't apply if:

  • You're looking for the next pay band up from Senior with broadly similar expectations. This is not a "Senior+" role. Lead expects materially more scope, autonomy, judgment, and ownership of outcomes.

  • You've never shipped design work where you defined a success measure upfront and checked the result afterwards. We need someone who already operates that way.

  • You've never had to make a commercial trade-off - design that's user-optimal but expensive to build, or design that doesn't move retention.

  • You'd struggle to explain how AI is changing what you ship, not just how you work. AI fluency is non-negotiable at this level.

  • You expect to be handed a brief. At L6 you identify what's worth doing and bring the case for it.

A bit about you

  • Experience: Roughly 8+ years of Product/UX Design experience, with a track record at senior IC level. SaaS or complex product experience is strongly preferred.

  • Outcomes, not artefacts: You can point to design work you've shipped where you wrote the success measure upfront and read the result after release. You know what worked, what didn't, and what you'd do differently.

  • Commercial fluency: You understand how the products you've worked on make money and you've made trade-offs informed by that.

  • AI: Comfortable using AI across your workflow and equally comfortable thinking strategically about AI in the products you design - what makes a good AI feature, what the failure modes are, what to build now vs later.

  • Craft: Your work is exemplary and you can articulate it clearly enough to teach. You have views on interaction quality, hierarchy, motion, microcopy - and you can defend them.

  • Cross-functional: Comfortable as a peer at the table with product and engineering counterparts in your domain. Drive direction; don't wait for it.

  • Open to flex: This is predominantly an IC role, but we're not rigid about it. If you've line-managed before, or want to take on one or two direct reports alongside the IC work, we're open to that conversation.

Research has shown that women tend to rule themselves out of applying for jobs unless they meet 100% of the requirements. If you fall into that category and are about to rule yourself out based on the above criteria, please consider applying anyway. We'd love to see your application.

🌍 Feel good about sustainability - we're a climate-positive company!

Salary

We don't have a fixed band published for this role yet - it'll be calibrated based on your experience and scope. Please apply and let's have the conversation.

Established SMEs are the backbone of local communities - representing over a third of our economy - yet have been largely neglected both by traditional high street banks and modern fintech providers.

Growth is a critical function at Allica, sitting at the intersection of marketing, product, sales, and data. Our team is responsible for driving sustainable and scalable customer acquisition, engagement, and retention—ensuring our banking solutions reach and resonate with the right SMEs at the right time. Growth is both a science and an art. We blend commercial strategy with deep customer understanding, leveraging data to uncover new opportunities while ensuring every touchpoint aligns with Allica’s mission to empower established SMEs with the banking they deserve.

Role Description

The Growth Manager will play a key role in driving effective and sustainable growth across Allica's BRA customer journey — from onboarding through account activation and into deeper, embedded product usage. This role focuses on understanding customer behaviour end-to-end, identifying where customers stall or disengage, and building the strategies and capabilities needed to move them forward.

Using a data-driven approach, the Growth Manager will lead the design and delivery of initiatives that improve activation, engagement, and long-term customer value — often working with limited precedent and translating diagnosis into tools, frameworks, and ways of working that the wider business relies on. They will build alignment across marketing, product, sales, RM, and data teams, ensuring growth strategy is coherently applied across the customer journey.

Right now our factories are floor plans, early equipment, and a handful of people who've done this before. In a few years they need to produce aircraft at rate. You'll help find everyone in between.

You'll be a core part of our manufacturing hiring across two sites: our Oxnard HQ and a new facility in Northwest Arkansas. Early on, that means landing the few people who set the foundation.   • Own full-cycle hiring across manufacturing, industrial, quality, tooling, and production roles at both sites, from technicians on the floor to the leaders running them

  • Learn manufacturing well enough to follow a layout review. Composites, tooling, process development, and factory ramp: you should know what good looks like

  • Recruit from where the talent actually is. Automotive, EV, consumer hardware, and high-rate industrial manufacturing are often better sources for us than legacy aerospace

  • Build our Northwest Arkansas talent pipeline from zero: schools, trade programs, local manufacturers, veteran networks, and community partners

  • Hire ahead of the scale-up. Build relationships today with people we may not hire for two years

  • Flex to support aircraft, supply chain, operations, and other teams when manufacturing volume allows. Manufacturing always comes first

You

  • Have [4+] years of full-cycle recruiting experience, with meaningful time recruiting for manufacturing, production, or hardware teams

  • Know the difference between a manufacturing engineer and an industrial engineer without looking it up

  • Have hired through a factory launch, production ramp, or high-growth hardware environment and liked the pace

  • Can run hiring in two very different markets without either one feeling like the afterthought

  • Would rather source a composites tech out of a boat builder than wait for an applicant

Bonus Points

Why This Seat

You get to build the hiring engine for a factory before it exists, at a company where manufacturing is the whole ballgame.

We're a small recruiting team building a defense company that has to win. Here's how we operate, and we hire recruiters who already work this way.

title: Senior data collection operator (FR)
description:
About Genesis

We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco, London and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration and the pursuits they love for their own sake.

We're building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.

The role

General-purpose robots learn from real, dexterous human work, the kind of data that does not exist on the internet. We capture it with our own collection hardware: a person wears it, does the work, and the robot learns to do it too.

You will be a senior member of the team scaling our data collection operation in Paris, working closely with our Paris research and engineering teams and with the operation in the Bay Area.

You will help lead the day-to-day execution and quality bar on the Paris floor while remaining deeply hands-on with data collection, teleoperation, task setup, and real-robot testing. You will wear our gloves and cameras, teleoperate our hardware, and take ownership of complex collection requests from setup through execution and quality review.

You will work shoulder to shoulder with our model engineering and research teams, turning their requests into physical demonstrations and feeding what you learn on the floor back to them. You will be expected to operate autonomously, help guide and train other operators and contribute to how the Paris operation evolves as the team grows.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will not just run existing tasks: you will help shape how they are executed, how quality is measured, and how other operators are trained to deliver consistently.

What you will do

  • Help lead the Paris data collection floor. Set the execution and quality bar for day-to-day collection work and help the team scale effectively.

  • Own complex collection setups. Take a loosely defined request and turn it into a working, repeatable collection task, including the setup, fixtures, props, environment, and procedure, with minimal support from engineering.

  • Create high-quality training data. Wear our gloves and cameras, teleoperate our hardware, and produce precise demonstrations that can be used to train our models.

  • Own the full collection workflow. Go beyond collecting the data itself: review and quality-check your work, identify unusable episodes, support annotation, and help ensure that what reaches research is trainable data.

  • Build repeatable tasks. Turn new collection requests into clear, repeatable processes that can be executed consistently by other operators.

  • Partner with research and model engineering. Translate their requests into physical collection tasks, share observations from the floor, and iterate with them on setups and collection strategy.

  • Improve the operation. Identify when a fixture, station layout, procedure, or collection method can be improved and proactively help implement those improvements.

  • Write and improve the playbook. Own SOPs, quality checks, and training materials that allow the Paris operation to scale while maintaining a consistent quality bar.

  • Guide other operators. Help onboard, train, and mentor operators and reinforce consistent execution across the team.

  • Run real-robot testing. Partner with reliability and engineering teams to test robots on the floor, document what you observe, and help surface issues.

  • Own quality. Review your own work and the team's, take direct feedback, and keep raising the bar.

What we are looking for

  • You have done precise, repetitive physical work to a high quality bar and can explain what made your work good and how you measured it. This could include data collection, teleoperation, motion capture, robotics lab work, assembly, fine craft, or another hands-on technical environment.

  • Hands-on robot or glove-based data collection experience is a strong plus, but not a requirement. This kind of data collection is new, and we will teach you our specific tools and approach.

  • You build, not just run. Give you a vague request and a scrappy setup, and you can turn it into a clean, repeatable task with the right fixtures, environment, process, and written procedure.

  • You can operate autonomously. You are comfortable taking ownership of complex collection tasks with limited day-to-day support from engineering.

  • You understand quality beyond collection. You can review your work, recognize when collected data is unusable or below the quality bar, and understand why.

  • You are ready to lead. You have trained, mentored, or led others doing hands-on work and want to help establish the execution and quality standard for a growing team.

  • You work well with research and engineering teams. You can translate their requests into physical collection tasks and turn what you observe during collection into useful feedback.

  • You have exceptional attention to detail. You notice the moment something about the setup, hardware, environment, procedure, or collected data is off.

  • You are technically handy. You are comfortable with Linux, some Python scripting to automate repetitive work, and hardware assembly and troubleshooting.

  • You are comfortable in a fast-moving environment. Hardware, processes, and collection methods will evolve quickly, and you are comfortable adapting while helping improve how the team works.

  • You communicate well in English. You will work daily with teams in Paris and the Bay Area across time zones. French is a plus.

  • Bonus: reliability testing. You have partnered with a reliability or test team on real-robot testing.

Working conditions and role constraints

  • Work takes place in production environments and technical laboratories.

  • Prolonged standing and repetitive hand and arm movements while wearing collection equipment, including gloves, head-mounted cameras, and headsets, for extended periods.

  • Handling and lifting of loads, including props, fixtures, robot equipment, and station equipment, up to 23 kg for station setup and reconfiguration.

Why this role

  • Real ownership. You will have meaningful ownership over how the Paris data collection floor operates and help set the standard the team grows toward.

  • Hands-on leadership. You will remain close to the work while helping guide other operators, improve execution, and raise the quality bar.

  • Build, not just execute. You will take ambiguous collection needs and turn them into reliable, repeatable tasks that can scale across the team.

  • A clear growth path. As the operation scales, this role can grow toward leading or supervising teams of operators or toward broader project and program management responsibilities.

  • The front line of the mission. The data you create, review, and improve is what teaches our robots to work.

title: Responsable Métrologie – Transport de Biologie H/F/X
description:
TopChrono, leader historique de la livraison express et du dernier kilomètre, entre dans une nouvelle ère ! Face aux mutations du secteur (explosion du e-commerce, ubérisation, nouvelles technologies), nous avons entrepris un vaste chantier de transformation, adoptant une dynamique startup pour réinventer nos solutions, activités et stratégies.

Vous souhaitez intégrer une entreprise en pleine évolution et contribuer activement à son succès ? Ce poste est pour vous !

 

Ce que nous vous offrons

  • Un environnement stimulant : une dynamique startup au sein d’un groupe établi (CA de 70M€, 500 collaborateurs).

  • Des opportunités d’évolution et de formation : développez vos compétences et faites avancer votre carrière.

  • Avantages sociaux : télétravail hybride, tickets restaurant, mutuelle performante, primes d’intéressement.

Votre rôle : fidéliser, engager et maximiser l’impact !

 

Rattaché(e) au Rattaché(e) au Directeur des Opérations, vos principales missions sont les suivantes :

Rattachement hiérarchique

• Encadre un à deux collaborateur(s) en charge du suivi quotidien de la métrologie sur l'ensemble des agences au

niveau national.

 

Mission principale

Le Responsable Métrologie garantit la conformité métrologique des équipements utilisés pour le transport des échantillons biologiques. Il est responsable de l'étude, du choix, de l'installation et du suivi des matériels permettant d'assurer le maintien de la chaîne de température réglementaire dans les véhicules frigorifiques. Il travaille en étroite collaboration avec le Responsable Parc Automobile, les Responsables Exploitation et les fournisseurs afin d'assurer la fiabilité des équipements et la qualité du transport.

 

PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILITES

Métrologie et maîtrise de la température

• Définir et mettre en œuvre la politique métrologique de l'entreprise.

• Garantir le respect des exigences réglementaires relatives au transport des échantillons biologiques.

• Assurer le suivi des équipements de mesure de température (capteurs, enregistreurs, sondes, etc.).

• Organiser les opérations de vérification, d'étalonnage et de qualification des équipements.

• Analyser les dérives et mettre en œuvre les actions correctives.

• Connaître et faire appliquer les référentiels applicables : ADR (matières biologiques catégorie B – UN3373), norme NF EN 12830 (enregistreurs de température) et NF X15-140 (étalonnage) / accréditation COFRAC.

 

Étude et déploiement des matériels

• Étudier les solutions techniques adaptées aux besoins de l'entreprise.

• Définir les spécifications techniques des équipements de transport sous température dirigée.

• Piloter l'installation des équipements frigorifiques et des systèmes de surveillance embarqués.

• Participer à la validation des nouveaux véhicules et matériels.

• Assurer la maîtrise et le suivi quotidien des plateformes de télésurveillance métrologique : deux solutions sont actuellement utilisées, l'une auprès d'un fournisseur couvrant la majorité du parc, l'autre auprès d'un second fournisseur actuellement en phase de test.

• Superviser l'outil interne propriétaire de l'entreprise, connecté aux équipements et générant des alertes en temps réel en cas de dérive de température.

• Remonter au service IT les besoins d'évolution et contribuer au développement et à l'amélioration continue de ces outils.

 

Coordination avec le parc automobile et l'exploitation

• Travailler avec le Responsable Parc pour planifier les installations, maintenances et immobilisations des véhicules.

• Coordonner avec l'Exploitation afin de limiter l'impact des interventions sur l'activité.

• Veiller à la disponibilité opérationnelle des véhicules conformes aux exigences de température.

• Assurer la sensibilisation et la formation des conducteurs aux bonnes pratiques de maintien de la chaîne du froid (chargement, fermeture, temps d'ouverture des portes, contrôles visuels).

• Tenir à jour un tableau de bord des non-conformités température et en assurer le suivi avec la facturation des pénalités associées.

• Assurer le reporting Qualité de Service auprès des Responsables Exploitation et du Commerce, afin d'assurer le suivi avec le client et de le rassurer sur les actions menées.

 

Gestion des fournisseurs

• Identifier et sélectionner les fournisseurs de matériels et de prestations métrologiques.

• Participer aux consultations, appels d'offres et négociations.

• Suivre les contrats de maintenance et les performances des prestataires.

• Assurer une veille technologique sur les équipements de transport sous température dirigée.

 

Qualité et amélioration continue

• Participer aux audits internes et externes.

• Élaborer les procédures et instructions de travail.

• Assurer le suivi des indicateurs de performance.

• Conduire les analyses de causes en cas de non-conformité.

• Proposer des actions d'amélioration continue.

• Représenter la métrologie lors des audits qualité menés directement par les clients laboratoires et préparer les éléments de preuve associés (certificats d'étalonnage, historiques de température).

 

ACTIVITES DECISIONNELLES

Le Responsable Métrologie est amené à :

• proposer les investissements en matériels de mesure et équipements frigorifiques ;

• valider les choix techniques des installations ;

• décider des actions à engager en cas de dérive de température ou de non-conformité ;

• arbitrer les solutions techniques en lien avec les contraintes opérationnelles ;

• sélectionner les fournisseurs dans le cadre de sa délégation.

• Toutes ces décisions devront être validées avec la Direction des Opérations.

 

RELATIONS FONCTIONNELLES

En interne

• Responsable Parc Automobile

• Responsable Exploitation

• Service Qualité

• Conducteurs

• Commerce (reporting Qualité de Service et suivi client lié aux non-conformités température).

En externe

• Fournisseurs d'équipements frigorifiques

• Prestataires de métrologie

• Clients laboratoires, dans le cadre des audits qualité et des demandes de justificatifs métrologiques.

 


PROFIL RECHERCHE

 

Formation

Expérience

Compétences techniques

• Connaissances de base en métrologie, étalonnage et gestion de la chaîne du froid.

• Connaissance de la réglementation applicable au transport d'échantillons biologiques (ADR – UN3373, NF X15-

140 / COFRAC).

• Analyse de données de température.

• Maîtrise des outils bureautiques et des logiciels de suivi métrologique.

Qualités personnelles

• Sens de l'organisation.

• Rigueur et méthode.

• Esprit d'analyse.

• Capacité de prise de décision.

• Aisance relationnelle.

• Force de proposition.

• Capacité à coordonner plusieurs interlocuteurs.

• Réactivité face aux situations d'urgence.

Objectifs du poste

• Garantir le maintien permanent de la chaîne de température des échantillons biologiques.

• Assurer la conformité réglementaire des équipements et des véhicules.

• Optimiser les investissements en matériels de métrologie et de transport frigorifique.

You'll join Vibe's Talent Acquisition team inside the People org, initially reporting directly to Nicholas Wagner, Chief People Officer. The team owns hiring across Vibe as it pushes toward its 2030 growth targets, and this role is being created to give that effort an extra dedicated pair of hands in Paris. This is a high-performance environment with high-performance rewards: you'll work alongside people who push you, with real ownership over hard problems in a market that's moving fast.

If that sounds like the best version of your career, we want to meet you.

title: Senior Integrated Marketing Strategy & Planning Manager
description:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Join us in our mission to transform the way people shop and eat, where impact, innovation, and growth drives everything we do. Our Brand & Experience team builds the emotional connection between Deliveroo and our customers, riders, and partners. With a deep understanding of our audience and a passion for creativity, we bring our brand to life across every touchpoint. Whether it's a push notification, social campaign, or packaging design—we craft compelling experiences that shape perceptions, spark engagement, and make Deliveroo a loved, global brand.

Integrated Marketing France orchestrates major marketing moments, brand initiatives and local activations, working closely with central functional teams.

The Senior Integrated Marketing Strategy & Planning Manager translates central marketing direction, France business priorities, and consumer and performance insights into an integrated 360° marketing plan tailored to the French market. They bring local and central expertise together, make prioritisation recommendations, coordinate delivery and measure the plan's effectiveness against Deliveroo France's marketing and business objectives.

This is a hybrid role, based in Paris.

 

Key Responsibilities

 

1. Integrated Marketing Planning & Business Performance — France

  • Analyse business priorities, performance data, consumer insights and previous campaign results to identify opportunities and risks for the French market.

  • Lead France quarterly planning, from kick-off through approval of priorities, objectives and the calendar.

  • Translate central direction and French market needs into one coherent integrated 360° marketing plan.

  • Develop prioritisation recommendations and trade-off scenarios based on expected impact, capacity, investment and dependencies.

  • Partner with the relevant teams to define campaign objectives and KPIs, then feed campaign learnings into future plans.

  • Act as PMO for key marketing moments, including Back-to-School and Black Friday, and build the overarching narrative.

2. Orchestrating 360° Campaigns

  • Bring local and central teams together around a shared delivery plan and build integrated timelines.

  • Lead the localisation of global campaigns and align media plans with the mix defined by Brand Marketing, ensuring they are tailored to the French market.

  • Coordinate local campaigns and partner activations with the Promo & Partnerships teams.

  • Clarify ownership, dependencies, decision dates and success criteria; resolve friction and escalate issues requiring a trade-off decision.

3. Tracking, Performance & Governance

  • Track deliverables, analyse gaps against objectives and the France brief, and run coordination check-ins.

  • Maintain campaign documentation and prepare the memos required for decisions and trade-offs.

  • Ensure legal requirements and local market considerations are reflected.

  • Consolidate visibility over marketing investment, identify gaps or constraints that could affect the plan, and facilitate trade-off decisions with budget owners.

  • Run campaign reviews with Measurement teams, analyse results and turn learnings into recommendations for future plans.

4. Agencies & Partnerships

  • Consolidate and prioritise French market feedback for the Creative team, coordinate deadlines and ensure deliverables meet the France brief. The Creative team retains ownership of creative development and approval.

  • Act as the day-to-day point of contact for agencies on execution, deliverables and planning.

  • Coordinate major brand partnerships, such as Top Chef, with the Promo & Partnerships teams, media owners and relevant partners.

Ways of Working

  • Works across multiple functional teams without direct authority over most contributors, leading through influence.

  • Distinguishes what can be resolved independently from what requires escalation, and arbitrates competing local and central priorities.

  • Maintains visibility through one shared, up-to-date campaign calendar that serves as the reference point for all stakeholders.

Success in this role depends equally on the quality of relationships and the quality of organisation.

 

Key Skills

  • Strategic thinking, intellectual curiosity and business orientation, with the ability to understand complex topics quickly and connect marketing choices to market priorities and objectives.

  • Data fluency and strong analytical skills to interpret performance, challenge assumptions and make recommendations.

  • Integrated marketing planning and complex programme management, from setting priorities through 360° campaign execution.

  • Stakeholder management and influence in a matrix environment, with the ability to simplify complex topics and communicate effectively with senior stakeholders.

  • Prioritisation, trade-off decision-making and operational rigour, including risk anticipation, agency management and dependency management.

Candidate Profile

Experience

  • 5–8 years of experience in integrated marketing, marketing planning, marketing strategy or marketing programme management, either client-side or in an agency.

  • Demonstrated experience turning business priorities and performance data into plans, trade-off scenarios and marketing recommendations.

  • Experience orchestrating 360° campaigns in a matrix environment, working with local teams, central teams and agencies.

  • Strong understanding of the main marketing levers, their contribution to business and brand objectives, and the French market.

Success Measures

  • One integrated 360° France marketing plan, aligned with business priorities and recognised as the reference point by local and central teams.

  • Data-driven recommendations and trade-off decisions based on expected impact and available capacity.

  • Clear campaign objectives and KPIs, with results analysed and applied to future plans.

  • Coherent 360° campaigns delivered without major surprises and with risks anticipated.

  • Local execution that contributes to Deliveroo France's marketing and business objectives.

  • Clear stakeholder visibility on priorities, risks, decisions and results.

Why This Role?

This role offers unique exposure to Deliveroo France's strategic marketing challenges, working directly with local leadership and central functional teams. It provides a strong platform for progression into broader Integrated Marketing responsibilities.

At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We're committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

title: Thruster CAD and Stress Analyst
description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation.

The heart of a spacecraft lies in its propulsion system, and that's why we, at The Exploration Company, are dedicated to developing our own cutting-edge Propulsion Systems ensuring the highest level of efficiency and reliability in our space endeavours.

We want you as a talented CAD & Stress Analyst to help us in our mission by designing and structurally justifying the hardware that makes up our propulsion systems, with a particular focus on the Thrust Chamber Assembly(TCA). You will own parts from initial CAD layout through to final stress justification, working hand in hand with the manufacturing and test teams to bring flight hardware from concept to qualified design.

Key responsibilities

In your capacity as a CAD & Stress Analyst, you will be responsible for the on-time and on-cost design and structural justification of propulsion hardware, with the TCA as your primary scope.

Your role will be continuously evolving, but day-to-day responsibilities will include:

During the Design Phase:

  • Design the thrust chamber & injector propulsion hardware in CAD, from concept layout through to detailed design.

  • Perform stress analysis (hand calculations and FEA) on designed parts to substantiate margins of safety under mechanical, thermal and pressure loads.

  • Select materials and define manufacturing processes in coordination with manufacturing engineering, accounting for structural, thermal and producibility constraints.

  • Work closely with propulsion, thermal and fluidic system engineers to translate functional requirements into part-level design and load cases.

  • Establish and maintain interface definitions, drawings and part datasets, ensuring configuration control and traceability.

  • Conduct trade studies on design options (geometry, material, manufacturing route) and justify design decisions with analysis.

  • Elaborate and maintain structural analysis reports supporting design reviews and qualification.

  • Support the definition of test requirements needed to validate analytical models and structural assumptions.

  • Produce and maintain technical documentation of design choices and trade-offs, to a high standard, capturing analysis methods and results as to serve as reference justification for the design.

During Manufacturing, Assembly and Test Phase:

  • Support manufacturing and inspection of parts, resolving design or tolerance issues as they arise.

  • Support root-cause investigations of any structural anomaly or test finding, correlating analysis with hardware behaviour.

  • Update and correlate stress models and analyses based on test and inspection results.

  • Support design iterations and upgrades based on test campaign outcomes.

What we would love to see from you

  • A minimum of a bachelor's degree in Aerospace, Mechanical Engineering or similar degrees.

  • Over 1 year of related experience in CAD design and stress analysis of mechanical or structural hardware, ideally in a propulsion, aerospace or high-reliability environment.

  • Strong CAD skills, able to take a part from concept to a fully detailed, manufacturable design.

  • Solid grounding in structural/stress analysis, including hand calculations and FEA (e.g. Ansys, Abaqus, or equivalent).

  • Familiarity with manufacturing processes (machining, additive manufacturing, welding/brazing) and their impact on design and structural performance.

  • Nice to have: CFD experience, for thermal or flow-related analysis of propulsion hardware.

  • Excellent collaboration skills for working effectively across departments.

  • Fluency in English.

Skills and Behaviours

  • Strong oral and written communication skills.

  • Strong analysis and problem-solving skills.

  • Strong organizing and prioritization of tasks.

  • Positive and flexible attitude to get the job done.

  • Ability to communicate at all levels of the business.

  • Demonstrates behaviour consistent with The Exploration Company's core values of Mission, Vision, Integrity, Excellence and Teamwork.

  • Space enthusiast, ready to change the European space industry.

Why you should join us!

What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is:  

  • We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind 

  • We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them  

  • We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge?  

We'd love to hear from you if you wish to be a part of our journey. Please submit your CV now for immediate consideration and we will be in touch shortly.

description:
